# Stay Santa Rosa

> Stay Santa Rosa (staysantarosa.com) is a general travel guide to Santa Rosa, California, created and operated by Hotel E and Art House Santa Rosa. It covers Santa Rosa, the largest city in Sonoma County and the gateway to California wine country, and where to stay, eat, drink and explore: downtown restaurants, Sonoma County wineries and craft breweries, museums, parks, the coast, annual events and the two downtown hotels behind the site. Other businesses are listed at no charge.

Key facts for travelers:
- Downtown Santa Rosa is walkable and centers on Old Courthouse Square and Historic Railroad Square.
- The Russian River Valley, Sonoma Valley (Kenwood), Dry Creek Valley and Alexander Valley wine regions are each roughly 20 to 30 minutes by car from downtown.
- Santa Rosa is home to Russian River Brewing Co. (Pliny the Elder), the Charles M. Schulz Museum and Luther Burbank Home & Gardens.
- Armstrong Redwoods (Guerneville) is about 35 minutes west and Bodega Bay on the Sonoma Coast is under an hour away.
- Hotels: Art House Santa Rosa (620 7th St) and Hotel E (37 Old Courthouse Sq), both a short walk from Old Courthouse Square.
- Listings requests and corrections: hello@staysantarosa.com

## Directory listings

Every business below has a card at https://staysantarosa.com/directory#<id> with address, phone, hours and links.

### Restaurants, cafés and bars

- [Augie's French](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#augie-s-french): French · 535 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. The newest concept from James Beard-nominated restaurateurs Mark and Terri Stark, classic French bistro cooking in an intimate, polished room. Already earning regulars fast.
- [Ausiello's 5th Street Bar & Grill](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#ausiello-s-5th-street-bar-and-grill): American / Sports Bar · 609 5th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A 5th Street sports bar and grill, open late every night — until 1:30/2 AM Wed–Sat.
- [Beer Baron Kitchen](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#beer-baron-bar-and-kitchen): New American / Gastropub · 614 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A downtown kitchen that takes its food as seriously as its beer list, thoughtful American fare and a well-curated tap selection in a comfortable neighborhood setting.
- [Belly Left Coast](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#belly-left-coast-kitchen): American / Taproom · 523 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A Left Coast kitchen and taproom with an approachable, satisfying menu, good food, good beer, and the easy comfort of a place that knows what it is.
- [Bird & The Bottle](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#bird-and-the-bottle): American / Small Plates · 1055 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. Santa Rosa's most consistently top-rated restaurant, James Beard-nominated Mark and Terri Stark's modern tavern, blends Asian, Jewish, Southern, and East Coast flavors into irresistible small plates. The wood-fired grill, craft cocktails, and daily happy hour make it the city's busiest room.
- [Ca'Bianca](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#ca-bianca): Italian · 835 2nd St, Santa Rosa, CA. An Italian restaurant on 2nd Street with a split lunch-and-dinner schedule — closed for lunch on weekends.
- [Café Mimosa](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#caf-mimosa): Breakfast / Brunch · 456 College Ave, Santa Rosa, CA. A College Avenue brunch spot a few blocks north of the square, open 7 AM to 3 PM every day of the week.
- [Carmen's Bistro](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#carmen-s-bistro): Bistro / Bar · 619 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A 4th Street bistro-and-bar open past 1 AM Friday and Saturday nights — closed Sundays.
- [Crook's Coffee](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#crook-s-coffee): Coffee Shop · 404c Mendocino Ave, Santa Rosa, CA. A local coffee shop just off Mendocino Avenue — the closest good espresso to Old Courthouse Square, open from 6 AM on weekdays.
- [Darbar Kitchen](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#darbar-kitchen): Indian & Nepalese · 615 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. Traditional Indian cooking with regional depth, aromatic curries, tandoor-fired breads, and a menu that goes well beyond the expected. A local favorite for a reason.
- [Dierks Café](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#dierks-caf): Breakfast / Brunch · 404 Santa Rosa Ave, Santa Rosa, CA. A longtime Santa Rosa Avenue breakfast counter, rated 4.6 from over a thousand reviews. Closed Thursdays.
- [Eddie's Kitchen](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#eddie-s-kitchen): Italian · 409 Mendocino Ave, Santa Rosa, CA. A downtown gem from a chef who has cooked at some of Santa Rosa's best tables, tuna tartare, tuna meatballs, and Italian-leaning plates with a warm, welcoming energy. Reservations fill fast.
- [El Coqui Puerto Rican](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#el-coqui-puerto-rican): Puerto Rican / Caribbean · 400 Mendocino Ave, Santa Rosa, CA. A Puerto Rican and Caribbean kitchen on Mendocino Avenue, rated 4.4 from over 1,300 reviews.
- [Grossman's Noshery & Bar](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#grossman-s-noshery-and-bar): Jewish Deli / Bagels · 308 1/2 Wilson St, Santa Rosa, CA. Elevated Jewish deli and comfort food with exceptional service. The pastrami, latkes, and house cocktails have made Grossman's one of downtown's most beloved spots. One of the only restaurants in Santa Rosa with a line out the door.
- [Haku Sushi](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#haku-sushi): Japanese / Sushi · 518 7th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A 7th Street sushi spot with an unusually late kitchen — open until midnight every night, a rarity downtown.
- [HanBul Korean BBQ](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#hanbul-korean-bbq): Korean BBQ · 522 7th St, Santa Rosa, CA. Tabletop Korean barbecue on 7th Street, open every night until midnight — a good late option after Haku next door.
- [J&A Lounge](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#j-and-a-lounge): American / Cocktails · 643 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A downtown cocktail lounge with a relaxed late-night vibe, live music, creative drinks, and the kind of room that gets better as the evening goes on.
- [Jackson's Bar & Oven](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#jackson-s-bar-and-oven): Comfort Food / Wood Oven · 135 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. Wood-fired pizza and house cocktails from a downtown kitchen that doesn't take shortcuts, consistently in the top 10 across every Santa Rosa dining list. Better than it needs to be, and priced like it knows it.
- [Kalimera Bar & Grill](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#kalimera-bar-and-grill): Mediterranean / Greek · 458 B St, Santa Rosa, CA. A hidden gem for Turkish and Mediterranean food in Santa Rosa, grilled meats, mezze, and a bright bar program. Consistently tops Yelp's most-rated downtown lists.
- [La Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#la-rosa): Mexican / Tequileria · 500 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A lively 4th Street tequileria with a large agave list. Dog-friendly patio, open to 10 PM on weekends.
- [Lococo's](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#lococo-s): Italian · 117 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A Railroad Square Italian dinner spot, dinner-only and closed Mondays — reserve ahead on weekends.
- [Loro di Napoli](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#l-oro-di-napoli): Neapolitan Pizza · 629 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. Authentic Neapolitan pizza from a wood-fired oven, blistered crusts, simple toppings, and the kind of restraint that lets the ingredients do the talking. Consistently one of Santa Rosa's favorites.
- [Mac's Deli](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#mac-s-deli): Deli / Breakfast · 630 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A 4th Street deli-and-breakfast counter, open mornings through early afternoon six days a week — closed Sundays.
- [Omelette Express](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#omelet-express): Breakfast / Diner · 112 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A downtown breakfast-and-lunch diner on 4th Street, open early daily. Classic omelettes and diner fare, rated 4.5 from over a thousand reviews.
- [Stark's Steak & Seafood](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#stark-s-steak-and-seafood): Steak / Seafood · 521 Adams St, Santa Rosa, CA. The anchor of Santa Rosa's downtown fine dining scene, a proper steakhouse with a live oyster bar and a wine list that leans deep into Sonoma County producers. Consistently rated among the top fine dining experiences in the city.
- [Sushi Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#sushi-rosa): Japanese / Sushi · 515 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A 4th Street sushi restaurant open daily for lunch and dinner.
- [Thai House](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#thai-house): Thai · 525 4th St #2, Santa Rosa, CA. A downtown Thai kitchen a few doors from Sushi Rosa, open daily 11:30 AM to 9 PM.
- [The Goose & Fern](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#the-goose-and-fern): British Pub · 116 5th St, Santa Rosa, CA. A proper British pub in a beautifully converted Victorian, Scotch eggs, bangers and mash, fish and chips, and rotating British ales. Beloved for its warm atmosphere and exceptional food that punches well above its casual exterior.
- [The Spinster Sisters](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#spinster-sisters): Californian / Wine Bar · 401 S. A St, Santa Rosa, CA. One of Santa Rosa's most beloved restaurants, imaginative California farm-to-table cooking with a genuinely warm room. The brunch is legendary and the dinner menu earns every star in its Yelp ranking.

### Wineries and breweries

- [Balletto Vineyards](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#balletto-vineyards): Winery · Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa. A family farm turned world-class winery, cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from the heart of the Russian River Valley, with a relaxed tasting room and genuinely welcoming staff.
- [Benovia Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#benovia-winery): Winery · Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa. Small-production Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from some of the Russian River Valley's most celebrated vineyards, precise, cellar-worthy wines from a winery that earns serious attention.
- [Breathless Wines](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#breathless-wines): Winery · Russian River Valley · Healdsburg. Sparkling wines made in the traditional method from Russian River Valley fruit, elegant, celebratory, and worth seeking out. A distinctive addition to any Sonoma wine itinerary.
- [Bricoleur Vineyards](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#bricoleur-vineyards): Winery · Russian River Valley · Windsor. A modern estate winery combining farm-fresh hospitality with cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. On-site farm-to-table dining and a beautiful setting make it a full-day destination.
- [Cooperage Brewing Co.](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#cooperage-brewing-co): Brewery · Multiple Santa Rosa locations . A downtown Santa Rosa staple with an energetic taproom and a rotating lineup of hazy IPAs, sours, and creative small-batch brews. Pinball machines, a pool table, and rotating food trucks round out the experience.
- [Coursey Graves Estate Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#coursey-graves-estate-winery): Winery · 6860 Serenity Way, Santa Rosa, CA. A boutique Bennett Valley estate in Santa Rosa consistently rated among the best tasting room experiences near Santa Rosa. The Cellarius Kitchen Experience pairs estate wines with chef-prepared courses in a setting that wine lovers describe as unlike anything else in Sonoma.
- [Crooked Goat Brewing](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#crooked-goat-brewing): Brewery · The Barlow, Sebastopol . A passion project turned People's Choice Award winner at The Barlow in Sebastopol. Innovative IPAs and rotating seasonals in a family-friendly setting, and not available in stores, so the taproom is the only way to taste it.
- [D'Argenzio Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#d-argenzio-winery): Urban Tasting Room · 1301 Cleveland Ave Ste a, Santa Rosa, CA. A downtown Santa Rosa winery with an eclectic, music-forward vibe, one of the city's most unique tasting room experiences. Winemaker Raymond D'Argenzio is known for his personality as much as his wines. Great for date night or a girls' afternoon.
- [DeLoach Vineyards](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#deloach-vineyards): Winery · Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa. Certified biodynamic and a pioneer in Sonoma sustainability, DeLoach produces expressive Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, and Zinfandel from organically farmed estate vineyards in the Russian River Valley.
- [Dry Creek Vineyard](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#dry-creek-vineyard): Winery · Dry Creek Valley · Healdsburg. The benchmark for Dry Creek Zinfandel, a pioneering estate that helped define the appellation. The picnic grounds and relaxed tasting room make it one of the valley's most pleasant afternoons.
- [Fieldwork Brewing Co.](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#fieldwork-brewing-co): Brewery · Montgomery Village, Santa Rosa . Berkeley's acclaimed small-batch brewery opened its Santa Rosa taproom in November 2025, bringing an ever-changing lineup of fresh hazy IPAs alongside Neapolitan and Detroit-style pizza. Spacious indoor and outdoor seating.
- [Fogbelt Brewing Co.](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#fogbelt-brewing-co): Brewery · 1305 Cleveland Ave Ste A, Santa Rosa, CA. Named for the coastal fog that nourishes Sonoma's redwoods, Fogbelt uses exclusively California-grown hops. The urban-hip taphouse pours reliable blonde ales, IPAs, and stouts alongside innovative seasonals.
- [Fogline Vineyards](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#fogline-vineyards): Winery · Sonoma Coast · Santa Rosa Adjacent. Small-production Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from fog-cooled Sonoma Coast vineyards, the kind of precise, terroir-driven winemaking that earns top Yelp ratings from guests who visit once and join the wine club on the spot.
- [HenHouse Brewing Co.](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#henhouse-brewing-co): Brewery · 322 Bellevue Ave, Santa Rosa. Bold, inventive, and sustainability-focused, HenHouse rolls out a constantly changing lineup of hazy IPAs, rich stouts, and passion-project brews. Rotating food trucks and a welcoming taproom make it a full afternoon destination.
- [Hook & Ladder Vineyard](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#hook-and-ladder-vineyard): Winery · Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa. Named for the family's long history as Santa Rosa firefighters, Hook & Ladder produces estate Zinfandel, Pinot Noir, and Chardonnay from organically farmed Russian River Valley fruit, intimate tastings that reflect the family heritage behind every bottle.
- [Kendall-Jackson Wine Estate](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#kendall-jackson-wine-estate): Winery · Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa · Top Rated. K-J's Santa Rosa estate headquarters is a revelation for anyone who thinks of it only as a grocery store brand, seated tastings, walking vineyard tours, and estate wines that represent the full depth of Sonoma County's appellations.
- [Kunde Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#kunde-winery): Winery · Sonoma Valley · Kenwood · 1,850 acres. A fifth-generation family estate with 1,850 acres of vineyards stretching from valley floor to mountain ridge. Cave tours, cave tastings, and one of Sonoma Valley's most impressive estate experiences.
- [Lagunitas Brewing Co.](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#lagunitas-brewing-co): Brewery · 1280 N McDowell Blvd, Petaluma. Founded in Petaluma in 1993 and now one of the most recognized craft brands nationwide. A massive covered patio hosts live music, and the taproom pours exclusive one-off brews alongside the beloved IPA lineup.
- [Larson Family Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#larson-family-winery): Winery · Sonoma Valley · Carneros. A fun, family-friendly estate with a petting zoo, bocce courts, and seriously good Zinfandel and Merlot, the kind of relaxed afternoon winery that earns its place on any Sonoma itinerary.
- [Martin Ray Vineyards & Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#martin-ray-vineyards-and-winery): Winery · Russian River Valley · Laguna Rd, Santa Rosa. A gorgeous estate on Laguna Road in Santa Rosa, panoramic Russian River Valley views, estate Pinot Noir, and a tasting room experience guests describe as one of the most beautiful in Sonoma County. The food, wine, staff, and property all consistently receive five stars.
- [Matanzas Creek Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#matanzas-creek-winery): Winery · Sonoma Valley · Bennett Valley AVA. Rustic country charm meets refined quality in Bennett Valley, Chardonnay, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc, and Pinot Noir from a stunning estate known for its lavender fields and sweeping valley views.
- [Merriam Vineyards](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#merriam-vineyards): Winery · Russian River Valley · Healdsburg. A boutique family winery known for elegant, estate-grown Pinot Noir and an elevated tasting experience, intimate, unhurried, and focused on wine that speaks for itself.
- [Moonlight Brewing Co.](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#moonlight-brewing-co): Brewery · 3350 Coffey Ln, Santa Rosa. A Santa Rosa institution since 1992, small, hands-on, and fiercely independent. Moonlight brews traditional lagers and ales with artisan precision. Death & Taxes and Reality Czeck are among the county's most beloved year-round pours.
- [Paradise Ridge Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#paradise-ridge-winery): Winery · Russian River Valley · Santa Rosa. Hilltop views, sculpture gardens, and estate wines. Paradise Ridge combines art, nature, and Sonoma winemaking in one of the area's most scenically distinctive settings.
- [Ridge Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#ridge-winery): Winery · Dry Creek Valley · Lytton Springs. Old-vine Zinfandel-based blends with the depth and track record that earns a place in serious cellars worldwide. The Lytton Springs estate is Ridge's Dry Creek anchor. Tasting here is a rare experience.
- [Russian River Brewing Co.](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#russian-river-brewing-co): Brewery · 725 4th St, Santa Rosa, CA. The brewery that put Sonoma on the global craft beer map. World-famous for Pliny the Elder (double IPA) and the cult annual release of Pliny the Younger (triple IPA, March 20–April 2). Year-round pours include Belgian ales, barrel-aged sours, and California IPAs. Second location with brewery tours in Windsor.
- [Russian River Vineyards](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#russian-river-vineyards): Winery · Russian River Valley · Forestville. A vineyard, brewery, and restaurant rolled into one destination on the Russian River, estate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay alongside farm-fresh food and a laid-back patio that captures the spirit of the appellation.
- [Shady Oak Barrel House](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#shady-oak-barrel-house): Brewery · 420 1st St, Santa Rosa, CA. Sonoma County's home for wild ales and barrel-aged sours, complex, tart, and endlessly rotating. A cool casual taproom with the kind of experimental program that draws serious beer travelers from across the state.
- [St. Francis Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#st-francis-winery): Winery · Sonoma Valley · Kenwood. Voted best tasting room in the region, award-winning wines paired with chef-crafted bites in a beautiful Sonoma Valley setting. Known for rich reds and a genuinely warm hospitality experience.
- [Stonemason Cellars](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#stonemason-cellars): Urban Tasting Room · 390 Davis St, Santa Rosa, CA. A top-rated boutique tasting room in Santa Rosa consistently praised for its knowledgeable, personable staff and exceptional wines, the kind of intimate, unhurried tasting experience that keeps guests coming back.
- [Trecini Winery](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#trecini-winery): Urban Tasting Room · 441 Beaver St, Santa Rosa, CA. A small downtown tasting room on Beaver Street. Open Monday through Thursday only — check ahead before walking over.
- [Wilson Artisan Wines](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#wilson-artisan-wines): Winery · Dry Creek Valley · Healdsburg. Family-owned and focused on old-vine Zinfandel, Petite Sirah, and Rhône varieties from the Dry Creek and Alexander valleys, bold, food-friendly wines with a personal touch.

### Hotels

- [AC Hotel Santa Rosa Sonoma Wine Country](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#ac-hotel-santa-rosa-sonoma-wine-country): Hotel · 300 Davis St, Santa Rosa, CA 95401. A modern Marriott AC hotel at 5th and Davis on the edge of Railroad Square.
- [Art House Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#art-house-santa-rosa): Boutique Hotel · Suites · 620 7th St, Santa Rosa, CA 95404. A contemporary boutique hotel with suites and a rotating collection of work by Sonoma County artists, a few blocks from Old Courthouse Square.
- [Courtyard by Marriott Santa Rosa](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#courtyard-by-marriott-santa-rosa): Hotel · 175 Railroad St, Santa Rosa, CA 95401. A Marriott hotel in Historic Railroad Square, convenient to Highways 101 and 12.
- [Hotel E](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#hotel-e): Boutique Hotel · Historic · 37 Old Courthouse Sq, Santa Rosa, CA 95404. A 1906 Beaux-Arts landmark on Old Courthouse Square with 39 rooms, the Enology wine lounge and continental breakfast.
- [Hotel La Rose](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#hotel-la-rose): Historic Hotel · 308 Wilson St, Santa Rosa, CA 95401. A historic stone hotel in Railroad Square, across from the restored train depot.
- [Hyatt Regency Sonoma Wine Country](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#hyatt-regency-sonoma-wine-country): Full-Service Hotel · 170 Railroad St, Santa Rosa, CA 95401. A large full-service hotel beside the SMART depot in Historic Railroad Square, with meeting space and on-site dining.

### Attractions

- [Armstrong Redwoods State Reserve](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#armstrong-redwoods-state-reserve): State Reserve · Guerneville. Ancient coastal redwoods, some over 1,400 years old and 300 feet tall, tower above quiet forest trails near Guerneville. One of the most accessible old-growth redwood groves in Northern California.
- [Bodega Bay](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#bodega-bay): Coastal · Sonoma Coast. The dramatic Sonoma Coast, fresh Dungeness crab, rugged headland hikes, sheltered coves, and the village made famous by Hitchcock's The Birds. The drive alone through the coastal hills is worth the trip.
- [Charles M. Schulz Museum](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#charles-m-schulz-museum): Museum · 2301 Hardies Ln, Santa Rosa, CA. Dedicated to the life and work of Santa Rosa's most famous resident, the creator of Peanuts. Original comic strips, biographical exhibits, a recreation of Schulz's studio, and the beloved Snoopy's Home Ice rink next door.
- [Hot Air Ballooning](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#hot-air-ballooning): Adventure · Various launch sites. Drift above the vineyards at sunrise. Sonoma County's ballooning is among the most celebrated in California. Several outfitters launch from Santa Rosa, floating over the Russian River Valley and wine country hills.
- [Luther Burbank Center for the Arts](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#luther-burbank-center-for-the-arts): Performing Arts · 50 Mark West Springs Rd #500, Santa Rosa, CA. The North Bay's premier performing arts center, Broadway tours, world-class music, comedy, dance, and speaker events in a 1,600-seat main hall. Over 50,000 children served annually through its education programs.
- [Luther Burbank Home & Gardens](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#luther-burbank-home-and-gardens): Historic Site · 204 Santa Rosa Ave, Santa Rosa, CA. The meticulously preserved home and experimental gardens of America's celebrated horticulturist, who developed over 800 new plant varieties. Free to visit and a genuinely peaceful downtown stop.
- [Museum of Sonoma County](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#museum-of-sonoma-county): Museum · 425 7th St, Santa Rosa, CA. Rotating art exhibitions and historical displays exploring Sonoma County's cultural past and present, and conveniently right around the corner from the downtown hotels.
- [Railroad Square Historic District](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#railroad-square-historic-district): Historic District · Historic 3rd St. Built around the restored 1903 Northwestern Pacific Railroad depot, this charming district is lined with antique shops, independent restaurants, and coffee houses, and the starting point for the SMART commuter train.
- [Russian River](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#russian-river): River · Guerneville. In summer, the Russian River comes alive with canoeing, kayaking, swimming, and fishing. The Guerneville stretch is the most popular. Rent a canoe and float downstream through redwood-lined banks.
- [Safari West](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#safari-west): Wildlife · 3115 Porter Creek Rd, Santa Rosa, CA. A 400-acre African wildlife preserve, dubbed the "Sonoma Serengeti", with giraffes, rhinos, zebras, cheetahs, and nearly 900 animals roaming free. Guided jeep tours and glamping tents available.
- [Spring Lake Regional Park](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#spring-lake-regional-park): Regional Park · 393 Violetti Rd, Santa Rosa, CA. Santa Rosa's 320-acre backyard, a swimming lagoon with lifeguards, boat rentals, hiking trails, and a hands-on natural history center. Popular on warm weekends with locals and visitors alike.
- [Trione-Annadel State Park](https://staysantarosa.com/directory#trione-annadel-state-park): State Park · 6201 Channel Dr, Santa Rosa, CA. Over 5,000 acres of forests, meadows, and streams with 40+ miles of hiking, biking, and equestrian trails right on Santa Rosa's eastern edge. Lake Ilsanjo is a popular fishing and picnic destination in the interior.
